name: The First Guess
tagline: Your questions are how everyone else starts looking.
epigraph: From around Cognac, where something growing on the walls was misnamed for over a century.
glassware: a small tulip-shaped glass (about 180 ml), chilled, no ice
language_row: Wren's Resonance on reading v3: ready. Line that lands: *When someone says "actually, nobody's really sure", most people sigh. You light up.* Swap test clean against *In a Minute*, *The Other Berry*, *Curtain Call* and *The Way It Felt*; 4-grams clean against every pour (five collisions moved off in v1, including "the next time a" and "stirred cold and served"). y5 "offer your guess" ("out loud" is *Curtain Call*'s). No Alice, mushrooms, yeast, veil, flor or sherry. "I like to think" twice, one sentence each. History 42% of yours. Pronouns he/him in y1–y3 are Baudoin, never the guest. ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/baudoinia-compniacensis.md` (F1–F19): *Oxford Companion* BAUDOINIA pdf 238 (also ANGEL'S SHARE pdf 110, MOLD pdf 1347; bibliographies pdf 444, 619); Scott, Untereiner, Ewaze, Wong & Doyle, *Mycologia* 99(4), July 2007 (the paper that named the genus, primary); BnF record of Baudoin's *Étude sur le nostoc des murs de Cognac* (1878) and his 1893 book on making cognac; Adam Rogers, *Wired*, 2011 (secondary). Peppercorn botany (dossier only): GBIF; Austin & Felger, *Economic Botany* 2008; Zhang & Wang, *IJMS* 2017. Drink: *Cocktail Codex* p. 74 (Pineau des Charentes); *Oxford Companion* MISTELLE pdf 1315, PINEAU pdf 1518, COGNAC pdf 546, 1404, GLASSWARE pdf 912; INAO/Qualisud control plan PCPineau/P300-8 (sugar floor; ageing); *Flavor Matrix* Grape pdf 140 (Sichuan peppercorn). Room notes: `work/innocent-explorer/`.
names_note: **The First Guess**, the room's pick (all three, round 5): it names the guest's guess said out loud, wrong or not, which is what Baudoin did; it stands only while no line calls Baudoin's guess the first (Hester's guard, held in v3). **The Next Question** (Tomás's first pick) is the runner-up for Robin: Wren moved off it because a question kept open for later is *In a Minute*'s ground. Also considered: *Better Than the Name*, *Filed Under Something Else*.
open_items: **Not veto-free (contains spice).** The Sichuan peppercorn steep (a faint tingle) puts the pour under the spice veto on the safe side. Wren accepted the cost for the tingle ("a small question on the lips"); the family floor was already met by *Night Light*. A veto-free version without the steep (lemon peel only) is in Tomás's draft history: same numbers.

**Two cellar organisms in one family (for Robin).** *Night Light* (innocent-caregiver) is the flor inside sherry casks; this is the black fungus on warehouse walls. Fenced both ways: this pour has no yeast, flor, film, sherry, cask interiors, "cover", "protect", white or veil (Oxford's own "a light black veil" is never used), and no sherry in the glass.

**Oxford gives the renaming as "the 1990s"; the naming paper is 2007** (Scott et al., *Mycologia*). Under the studio's rule the reading gives no decade: "misnamed for over a century", "more than a century later".

**"First brought it to scientists' attention"** is Rogers' account (*Wired* 2011, secondary) of why the 2007 team honoured Baudoin. Baudoin "brought it to" the botanists of his day; he never "identified" it. The 1872 *Xenodochus* suggestion came from two botanists, before his 1878 nostoc, so no line calls his guess the first.

**Pineau's acid is unsourced** (no legal minimum on any page); the spec sits at the middle (0.45%), and acid reads OUT at 0.3% and 0.6% with a Pineau at either end. Sugar has the AOC floor (120 g/L); every point from 12 to 16 g balances.
**The tulip holding the scent** is craft, unsourced: stated in y4 as Wren's intent and signposted ("I like to think").
**Closing-line alternative for Robin:** *Name the tingle before anyone tells you what it is. A wrong name counts.* (Wren, round 5; withdrawn in favour of *Ask…*, kept in Tomás's draft).
